_note: Disha Quest: the first game every new student plays. 8 zones, one per ability, about 10-12 minutes. 'answer' and 'explanation' are never sent to the app.

abilities.label: Logical reasoning
abilities.description: Spotting rules and patterns, and following them step by step
abilities.growthTip: Try number and letter puzzles, or Sudoku, for 10 minutes a day.

abilities.label: Numerical ability
abilities.description: Working quickly and accurately with numbers, percentages and data
abilities.growthTip: Practise everyday maths: discounts, bills, speed and time.

abilities.label: Verbal reasoning
abilities.description: Understanding words, meanings and what a passage really says
abilities.growthTip: Read one news article a day and summarise it in two lines.

abilities.label: Spatial reasoning
abilities.description: Picturing shapes, rotations and how things fit in space
abilities.growthTip: Try tangrams, origami, LEGO or drawing objects from different angles.

abilities.label: Working memory
abilities.description: Holding information in mind and recalling it accurately
abilities.growthTip: Play memory card games, or recall your day in order before bed.

abilities.label: Critical thinking
abilities.description: Questioning claims, finding weak points and judging evidence
abilities.growthTip: When you see an ad or a forward, ask: what evidence is missing?

abilities.label: Creative thinking
abilities.description: Coming up with many different, original ideas
abilities.growthTip: Every day, list 5 new uses for an ordinary object.

abilities.label: People skills
abilities.description: Understanding others and handling situations with care
abilities.growthTip: In group work, try leading one discussion and listening first.

zones.name: Pattern Peaks
zones.intro: Every pattern hides a rule. Find it.

items.question: What comes next? 3, 6, 11, 18, 27, …
items.explanation: The gaps grow by 2: +3, +5, +7, +9, so next is +11 = 38.

items.question: Which letter comes next? B, E, I, N, …
items.explanation: The gaps grow by 1: +3, +4, +5, +6, so N + 6 = T.

items.question: All painters in the club are left-handed. Some left-handed people play chess. Which statement MUST be true?
options: None of these must be true
items.explanation: The chess players who are left-handed may or may not include painters, so nothing is certain.

items.question: A school bag costs ₹800 and has a 25% discount. How much do you pay?
Riya scored 18 out of 25 in Maths and 34 out of 50 in Science. In which subject did she do better?
A train covers 180 km in 2 hours 30 minutes. What is its average speed?
Pilot is to aircraft as captain is to …
items.explanation: A pilot commands an aircraft; a captain commands a ship.

items.question: Which word does NOT belong?
items.explanation: Timid means shy or fearful; the others mean courageous.

items.question: Arjun's phone battery lasts a full day in winter but only half a day in summer. He uses it the same way all year. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Arjun uses his phone more in summer
Heat may be reducing his battery life
items.explanation: Usage is the same, so the change in season (heat) is the likely cause.

zones.name: Shape Shift
zones.intro: Turn shapes in your mind. No flipping allowed!

items.question: Which option is the same shape, only rotated (not flipped)?
items.explanation: Option B is the shape turned 90° clockwise. The others are mirror images.

items.question: Which option is the same shape, only rotated (not flipped)?
items.explanation: Option C is the shape turned upside down (180°). The others are mirror images.

items.question: A wooden cube is painted red on every side, then cut into 27 equal small cubes. How many small cubes have exactly 2 red faces?
items.explanation: Cubes with 2 painted faces sit in the middle of each of the 12 edges.

zones.name: Memory Vault
zones.intro: Watch the lights, then tap them back from memory.

items.question: Remember which squares light up.
Harder: more squares, same time.

zones.name: Truth Tower
zones.intro: Not every claim is true. Find the weak spot.

items.question: Students who eat breakfast get better marks, so a school says breakfast makes students smarter. What's the biggest problem with this reasoning?
options: Something else, like more sleep or support at home, could explain both
items.explanation: Two things happening together doesn't prove one causes the other.

items.question: An ad says: "9 out of 10 users love our app!" Which question matters most before you believe it?
options: How many users were asked, and how were they chosen?
items.explanation: If only 10 happy users were asked, the claim means very little.

items.question: Claim: "Our town needs a new flyover because traffic is bad." Which fact would WEAKEN this argument the most?
options: Traffic is worst near the market
Most jams are caused by trucks parked on the road, which a flyover won't fix
Flyovers take two years to build
items.explanation: If the cause is parked trucks, a flyover doesn't solve the real problem.

zones.name: Idea Forge
zones.intro: There are no wrong answers here. Only more ideas.

items.question: How many different uses for an empty plastic bottle can you think of? One idea per line.

zones.name: People Plaza
zones.intro: Real situations. What would you do first?

items.question: Your project partner hasn't done their part, and the deadline is tomorrow. What do you do first?
options: Do their part yourself and say nothing
Message them privately to ask what's going on and plan together
items.explanation: Talking privately first solves the problem and keeps the relationship.

items.question: A new student sits alone at lunch every day and looks upset. What's the best first step?
options: Leave them alone; it's not your business
Invite them to sit with your group
Ask others why they're always alone
Post about it to raise awareness
items.explanation: A friendly invitation helps directly and respects their privacy.
